reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Nov 12 close, data fresh: SPX 7,592.40 is 3.21% off its 120-day high, 1.03% below its 50-day and 3.48% above its 200-day; SMH $501.73 printed Zone 2 ($470-505), 25.32% off its high and 10.58% below its 50-day; NVDA $166.19 is BELOW_ZONE_2 after closing below the $175 floor, 31.71% off its high; VIX 18.70 has rolled over from a 5-day high of 25.64; HY OAS 3.3 is calm; mechanical tally 3 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: The Probe stance is wrong if SMH closes below $470 without holding Zone 2, or if HY OAS breaks above 4% or VIX closes above 25 — either voids the probe and re-grades the episode as a regime break. It is also wrong if NVDA reclaims $175 while SMH holds Zone 2 and the tally holds at 3 of 4: that is a bottoming process, not a single probe, and the stance should step up to Add on the confirmed print.

ladder.response: Re-arm Tranche A: 25% deployment on the confirmed SMH Zone 2 print, sized to the print, not the intraday dip
ladder.trigger: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX below 25 and mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better — printed Nov 12 at $501.73 with tally 3 of 4 and VIX 18.70

ladder.response: Probe is void on the SMH leg; no averaging down — wait for the next zone print or a confirmed bottom before any deployment
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA closes below $160

ladder.response: Treat as the failed first bounce — no chasing, no new probes; wait for the second low to form and hold before any deployment
ladder.trigger: SMH or SPX bounces into the failure zone (SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820) and fails to hold a close above it

ladder.response: Stand down: no new probes, Tranche A re-arm is void, and the correction is re-graded as a regime break
ladder.trigger: HY OAS breaks above 4% or VIX closes above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day average ($7,337.35)

ladder.response: Tranche C conditions met: 50% deployment on the confirmed bottom, per the ladder
ladder.trigger: Confirmed bottom: failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds, with the 10-year yield falling — or a held close above SPX $7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail setup is the live risk: SMH printed Zone 2 at $501.73 but on only 0.82x average volume with no climax, and NVDA fell 4.34% to $166.19 the same day — a zone print without capitulation volume after a 31.71% NVDA drawdown is exactly where bull traps form. Entries wait for the zone to HOLD on the next close, not the print alone; no chasing the first bounce, and any rally into the SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 failure zone is judged on whether it holds a close above it, not on the size of the up day.

strategyPosture: Probe. SMH printed Zone 2 ($501.73) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4, VIX rolled over to 18.70 and credit calm — the re-arm print the ladder was waiting for has arrived. The probe is sized to the confirmed SMH print only: NVDA is still below its $175 floor and volume did not climax, so this is a probe, not an Add.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and concentrated in the names that dominate the index by weight — NVDA alone is 31.71% off its high — so index-level calm masks real damage underneath. But a rollover needs credit stress or a 200-day break, and neither is present: HY OAS is 3.3 and SPX sits 3.48% above its 200-day. Position as rotation: leadership is changing, not collapsing.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 3.1% off its 52-week high and -1.59% over one month, while the Mag 7 average sits 16.21% off their highs — a 13.11-point divergence gap. Credit is calm: HY OAS is 3.3% and bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). SPX closed Nov 12 at 7,592.40, just 1.03% below its 50-day average and 3.48% above its 200-day. The 10-year is 4.98% with a 2s10s curve of +0.25 — no inversion signal.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — Mag 7 Weakness Inside a Calm Index
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: the Magnificent 7 are deep off their highs and the AI complex is down 25% from its peak, so the index must be rolling over.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SPX closing below its 200-day average ($7,337.35) would convert rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: The price says the AI cycle is over; the revenue lines say the cycle is still compounding and the market is repricing the multiple, not the demand. The split inside the complex is the tell: AVGO rose 5.55% today on revenue growing 55% year over year while NVDA fell 4.34% on an acute catalyst — the market is sorting durable infrastructure from headline-exposed names. SMH printing Zone 2 without volume climax means the print is real but unconfirmed: the probe is earned, the bottom is not.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH closed Nov 12 at $501.73, inside Zone 2 ($470-505) and 25.32% off its 120-day high, 10.58% below its 50-day. NVDA closed at $166.19, below the $175 Zone 2 floor, 31.71% off its high with an RSI of 25.1 — deeply oversold — and the decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST, not deteriorating demand: NVDA revenue is still growing 61.4% year over year. MU sits at $793.59, 36.8% off its high with an RSI of 43.7. The mechanical tally is 3 of 4: zone occupancy, VIX rollover and credit calm confirmed; volume climax not confirmed (SMH volume 0.82x its 20-day average).
themes.label: AI Semis — SMH Prints Zone 2, NVDA Still Below Its Floor
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken: NVDA is down 23.5% over 20 days and fell 4.34% today on an acute catalyst, and the AI complex is repricing hard.
themes.watchFor: NVDA reclaiming $175 on a close with SMH holding inside Zone 2 ($470-505) repairs the Nov 9 bottom void and confirms the probe case across the complex.

themes.counterRead: The basket-wide selloff treats VST as a momentum proxy for the AI power narrative, but the fundamentals that matter — revenue growing 19.1% year over year and insiders buying $1.17M at the trough — point the other way. The gap between the basket's price action and VST's own numbers is the opportunity; the risk is that the power trade was always a derivative of the AI capex narrative, so a deeper AI repricing drags it regardless. VST is already a holding, so the read is about the next leg, not a new position.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the conviction promotion of this run (score 83): $133.97, -29.2% from its peak, revenue growing 19.1% year over year, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. The nuclear basket is selling off with it: CCJ -11.85%, GEV -13.22%, OKLO -15.56%, SMR -16.47% over one month.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power — VST at the Trough With Insiders Buying
themes.narrative: Power names rode the AI data-center story up and are now giving it back: VST is 29.2% off its peak and the whole nuclear basket is selling off with it as the AI capex narrative reprices.
themes.watchFor: VST closing below $130 with the nuclear basket still falling says the trough is not holding; VST reclaiming its 50-day average with the basket stabilizing arms the next leg.

themes.counterRead: The market is pricing a software demand collapse that the revenue lines do not show: DDOG's revenue inflection is RECOVERY, not deterioration. The divergence is the setup — but NOW's own revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING, so the theme is not uniform and names have to be picked on their own numbers, not the sector's. The dislocation list is dominated by sentiment-driven declines, not by deteriorating revenue.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is the top conviction name (score 82, tier A): revenue growing 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow (29.2% margin), while the stock sits 38.7% below its high with an RSI of 31.5. NOW is 42.2% off its high at $101.14 with an RSI of 30.1. ONTO (score 79) has revenue growing 41.5% year over year while 45.7% below its high. The dislocation list runs 31 names deep, 21 of them SENTIMENT_DRIVEN and 13 of them FULL_SIGNAL.
themes.label: Software / SaaS — Revenue Recovering While Prices Fall
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is the new crowded short: NOW is 42.2% off its high, DDOG 38.7%, and the sector reads as the next leg of the AI unwind as customers cut spend.
themes.watchFor: DDOG holding above $180 into its Jan 14 earnings window with no pre-announcement, or NOW's next print confirming the DETERIORATING inflection — either would settle whether this is repricing or real demand damage.

themes.counterRead: The narrative ran ahead of the fundamentals: treasury premiums and 2x leverage only work while Bitcoin rises, and with BTC down double digits the premium becomes a liability that compounds the fall. CONL at -46.31% in a month is leverage doing exactly what leverage does. Nothing in the input shows a fundamental turn — the washout is the price catching down to a narrative that had run too far, and holdings here are exposure to be sized, not averaged down into.
themes.dataAnchor: The unwind is broad and fast: over one month BTC-USD is -12.25% (-3.49% today), COIN -24.23%, BMNR -17.3% (-4.37% today), and CONL -46.31% (-7.75% today). BMNR and CONL are holdings. IBIT is -12.67% and ETH-USD -15.72% over the same month, so this is not a single-name problem — the whole crypto complex is de-rating together while the 10-year sits at 4.98% and real yields at 2.74%. TQQQ, the other leveraged holding, is -19.07% over one month.
themes.label: Crypto / Leverage Washout — the Premium Is Unwinding
themes.narrative: Crypto treasury and leveraged products were the cycle's easy leverage: CONL, BMNR, and DOGE let holders ride Bitcoin with a premium attached, and the premium was the trade.
themes.watchFor: BTC-USD stabilizing above its one-month range with IBIT flows turning positive for a full week would mark the washout ending; another leg down in BTC with CONL falling faster than 2x says leverage is still unwinding.

QQQ sits 0.24% above the Labs sell line, so the tape's next leg is decided in the same names.
